rti|tele-data-and-Introduction: The Telecommunications (Interception and Access) Act 1979 (Cth) (the Act) specifies circumstances where an Authorising Officer may make an authorisation for the disclosure of telecommunications metadata / prospective data from a telecommunications company to the WA Police. In October 2015 changes were made to the Act which specified new extra considerations which Authorising Officers now need to make when considering authorising a request for either metadata or prospective data. Section 180F now requires officers to consider the merit of the invasion of privacy in addition to the consideration of the purpose of the information being used under Sections 178, 178A, 179 & 180.
rti|tele-data-and-Authorising-Officers: Authorising Officers are delegated under Section 5AB(1) of the Act. A delegation schedule (attached) provides a list of positions within WA Police with delegated authority pursuant to s5AB(1) provided by the Commissioner of Police. This means that any officer acting into the position specified under the declaration is empowered to authorise disclosures for telecommunications metadata and prospective data under sections 178, 178A, 179 and 180 of the Act. Although provided legislative authority via the s5AB(1) delegation, Authorised Officers within the WA Police Force must also: Complete the Telecommunications Interception Compliance course located on the eForce learning platform (must complete every 24 months): Complete Authorising Officer Declaration and provide to Special Operations Application Unit: In the case of an officer acting in an Authorising Officer’s position, ensure Higher Duties is submitted on SIMR to reflect the appropriate position: Authorising Officers must ensure and demonstrate appropriate consideration is given to relevant areas when authorising telecommunications requests under Sections 178, 178A, 179 & 180 of the Act. The specific areas for consideration are provided within this document and should be read and understood by all persons performing an Authorising Officer function. A recent decision in the Supreme Court of Victoria in the matter of DPP v Osman, [2024] VSCA 210, provides an Authorising Officer with insight into their obligations under the Act. In the event of a rejection, the Authorising Officer is required to fill in a rejection slip / the reasons field in IDM, detailing the reasons for the rejection providing feedback for the requesting officer. This also allows WA Police Force to show Authorising Officers are complying with their obligations under the Act. If a request is deemed acceptable and is subsequently authorised, the Authorising Officer must note what time the authorisation was made on the hardcopy certificate (auto recorded in IDM). For authorisations under section 180 of the act, the Special Operations Applications Unit (SOAU) require all authorised certificates to have a statement from the Authorising Officer stating that they have considered privacy implications and are satisfied it meets the legislative standards required. For data to be requested to assist with an arrest warrant, there must be an active investigation (IMS I/R), always check the warrant is still outstanding prior to authorisation. If the suspect is arrested prior to authorisation, the request must be revoked. Extra scrutiny should be applied to bulk data, named variations, address checks and victim related requests, due to the increased risk of privacy concerns.
rti|tele-data-and-Case-Officer: To assist Authorising Officers when making the required considerations, case officers are required to ensure all available information is provided within data applications. This enables an Authorising Officer to better assess the request as per the requirements of the Act. Case officers are also required to include specific information including Incident Report (IR) numbers, CAD Job numbers, operation name and IDM reference numbers into the application which will assist Authorising Officers in locating the relevant information required to make an accurate determination. The Case Officer’s application must provide the following information: The offence being investigated linked to the data requested, The Act and Section for the offence, The fine or term of imprisonment for the offence, A date and time range which is relevant/restricted to the offence under investigation and Details provided must match the offence being investigated. If the original need for the data request no longer exists and no data has been returned, the requesting application must be cancelled. The risk of this occurring increases when data is requested in relation to assisting with actioning an arrest warrant. When making a request for bulk data, information must be provided to demonstrate the need for the data and what actions have been taken to minimise the amount of data requested.
rti|tele-data-and-Data-Types: ALL TELCO DATA IS TO BE STORED IN IDM AS IT’S USE MUST BE AUDITABLE AND TRACKED.
rti|tele-data-and-Metadata: Metadata is historic telecommunications data which is required to be kept under the Act by telecommunications companies. Types of communications include: IPND, Subscriber, CCR and RCCR communications which are requested under section 178, 178A or 179 of the Act. (Historic Non-content data)
rti|tele-data-and-Prospective-Data: Prospective data is future / live telecommunications data which is required to be provided under the Act by telecommunications companies. Types of communications include: Live Call Data, Cell-Associated Data (CAD) and Location Based Service / Triangulation (LBS). These are requested under section 180 of the Act. (Ongoing Non-content data)
rti|tele-data-and-Section-178: Section 178 specifies that an Authorising Officer cannot make an authorisation under this section unless they are satisfied that the information being requested is reasonably necessary for the purpose of enforcing criminal law. An authorised officer must not approve a request submitted pursuant to s178 for a Cell Tower Data Dump Quote, or court statements requested on a s178(2) form.
rti|tele-data-and-Section-178A: Section 178A specifies that an Authorising Officer cannot make an authorisation under this section unless they are satisfied that the information being requested is reasonably necessary for the purpose of locating the missing person.
rti|tele-data-and-Section-179: Section 179 specifies that an Authorising Officer cannot make an authorisation under this section unless they are satisfied that the information being requested is reasonably necessary for the purpose of enforcing an offence carrying a pecuniary penalty or for the purpose of protecting the public revenue.
rti|tele-data-and-Section-180: Section 180 specifies that an Authorising Officer cannot make an authorisation under this section unless they are satisfied that the information being requested is reasonably necessary for the purpose of the investigation of a ‘serious offence’ or an offence against a Commonwealth / State / Territory law with a maximum penalty of imprisonment of at least 3 years.
rti|tele-data-and-Section-180F: Before an authorised officer issues a data authorisation, he or she must be satisfied on reasonable grounds that any interference with the privacy of any person(s) is justifiable and proportionate, having regard to certain matters including: the gravity of any conduct in relation to which the authorisation is sought, including ; the seriousness of any offence in relation to which the authorisation is sought ; the seriousness of any pecuniary penalty in relation to which the authorisation is sought; the seriousness of any protection of the public revenue in relation to which the authorisation is sought ; whether the authorisation is sought for the purposes of finding a missing person; the likely relevance and usefulness of the information or documents; and the reason why the disclosure or use concerned is proposed to be authorised . Gravity, Relevance, Offence, Use, Privacy (GROUP) These considerations must be explicitly dealt with in the data authorisation request by both the case officer and the Authorising Officer. The amount of detail required will depend on the extent to which an individual’s privacy is being infringed and the seriousness of the offence being investigated. The Authorising Officer may consider imposing a ping rate as a condition of authorisation for Location-based Services, but otherwise, the Authorising Officer and the Investigating Officer should discuss considerations for variations in the ping rate, in accordance with operational requirements. In addition to the Investigating Officer recording this action in their Investigation Running Sheet or Investigation Action Register (IAR), a formal email will be required to be sent to SOAU mailbox for record keeping of any adjustment/s in frequency.
rti|tele-data-and-Verbal-Authorisations: Verbal Authorisations must not be provided by an Authorising Officer in respect to applications submitted pursuant to Sections 178, 178A, 179 & 180 of the Act. Although a verbal briefing may be provided to an Authorising Officer, notes and records must be made to demonstrate privacy considerations, relevancy of the data/information sought and the gravity of offence under investigation. A request may only be submitted to a service provider upon endorsement of the relevant Chapter 4 authorisation (Sections 178, 178A, 179 & 180) document. Although electronic signatures are permitted under the Act, the WA Police have only limited ability to provide electronic endorsement to applications at this time.
rti|tele-data-and-Cell-Tower-and-Payphon: In order to limit privacy intrusion to the maximum extent, Authorising Officers are required to provide additional scrutiny when considering authorisation of Cell Tower Data Dump and Payphone Data Dump requests. A Cell Tower/Payphone Data Dump request (unlike most other data requests) seeks a significant volume of data from a large number of persons, many or most of whom are not suspected of having committed a serious criminal offence. A Cell Tower/Payphone Data Dump request presents a significant intrusion to the privacy of a large number of persons, for this reason Authorising Officers must ensure the requested parameters are consistent with the aims of the investigation. In circumstances where an offence under investigation has been identified to have occurred at a specific time/date, an investigator seeking excessive Cell Tower/Payphone Data Dump periods (i.e., 24 hours) should be questioned and must provide detail as to why such a significant time parameter has been requested. In the event a case officer cannot justify the time parameters requested for a Cell Tower/Payphone Data Dump, the request shall be rejected by the Authorising Officer. Case officers shall upon receipt of Cell Tower/Payphone Data Dump, be provided advice in regard to the management and quarantine process for data which is identified as of no value or outside of the needs of the investigation. SOAU will review all Cell Tower/Payphone Data to ensure the data provided by the carrier is within the authorised date/time frame. In some circumstances the carrier may provide data outside of the period of authorisation requiring SOAU to immediately quarantine all unauthorised data, thereby providing the case officer with only data covered by the authorisation.
rti|tele-data-and-Cell-Tower-Data-Dump-Q: Applications submitted by WA Police for Cell Tower Data Dump Quotes are not permitted under s178 of the Act. Such requests are to be entered onto SEDNode with no legislation recorded as authority for the request as this type of request does not require s178 authority. In any instances where an application for a Cell Tower Data Dump Quote is submitted via SEDNode and a s178 authorisation is attached, the responsible staff member must: Email the Service Provider requesting the application is cancelled Re submit application via SEDNode without s178 authorisation Ensure the request including s178 authorisation is not recorded within legislative reporting figures. An Authorising Officer must not authorise a s178 request for a Cell Tower Data Dump Quote.
rti|tele-data-and-WA-Police-Telecommunic: Within the WA Police Force, the following areas are approved to facilitate and provision Telecommunications Data Requests under Sections 178, 178A, 179 & 180 of the Act.
rti|tele-data-and-Special-Operations-App: SOAU are the WA Police primary area responsible for the authorisation, provisioning, dissemination and compliance with telecommunications data pursuant to Sections 178, 178A, 179 & 180 of the Act. SOAU manage the WA Police TI Platform (JSI) and provision all TI warrants for the agency. SOAU are responsible for the compliance associated with all live TI obtained and also facilitate live TI warrants on behalf of the Internal Affairs Unit (IAU). SOAU also manage the majority of telecommunications data applications (metadata and prospective data). Case officers submit Request for Information (RFI) via the WA Police IDM system which is received by SOAU, processed and forwarded to an Authorising Officer for consideration. Upon authorisation SOAU prepare the request which is submitted to the service provider. Direct contact with service providers should always be conducted through SOAU. Once received, the data is vetted and disseminated back to the case officer via IDM. SOAU maintain all records and provide the central point of contact for all Ombudsman inspections relating to telecommunications data. Routine Prospective Data (PD) and Location Based Service (LBS) applications are also facilitated by SOAU however authorisation of these applications (routine) will be performed by the case officer’s respective division or portfolio.
rti|tele-data-and-State-Operations-Contr: SOCC Inspectors are delegated as per s5AB(1) as Authorising Officers and have the ability to consider and authorise applications submitted under sections 178, 178A, 179 & 180 of the Act. The SOCC will only facilitate authorisation and provision of requests outside of business hours when SOAU staff are unavailable. In circumstances where SOCC provide 5AB(1) authorisation of an application and SOAU facilitate/provision the request and provide results to a case officer, SOAU shall be responsible for compliance and maintaining records and documents for ombudsman inspection. In circumstances where SOCC provide 5AB(1) authorisation, facilitate/provision the request and provide results to the case officer, the SOCC shall be responsible for compliance and maintaining records and documents for ombudsman inspection. SOCC staff may authorise and facilitate requests submitted pursuant to section 286, 287, such as IPND checks for Persons at Risk (PAR). SOCC trained staff have the required access to SEDNode / OSTRAVA to facilitate such requests (upon authorisation) and provide results to the case officer. In doing so SOCC shall be responsible for vetting, compliance and maintaining records and documents for ombudsman inspection. SOCC staff must comply with all internal SOPs for the use of provisioning systems.
rti|tele-data-and-Internal-Affairs-Unit-: Staff attached to IAU perform telecommunications data authorisations pursuant to sections 178, 178A, 179 & 180 of the Act. IAU utilise Authorising Officers from within the Professional Standards Portfolio as per delegation under s5AB(1). IAU will authorise and facilitate telecommunication data requests (excluding TI warrants and Section 180) and are required to maintain all records and documents associated with such requests and make available for ombudsman inspection as required. It is accepted IAU may adopt localised practices and processes regarding the dissemination, storage and restriction of access to telecommunications data/information (given the nature of investigations undertaken) however, all processes, considerations and activities undertaken by case officers and Authorising Officers must be in accordance with the WA Police Force Telecommunications Data and Authorising Officers Standard Operating procedures. The IAU utilise SOAU for all s180 applications and TI warrants however will communicate such requests directly via the OIC of SOAU or Assistant Divisional Officer (ADO), who will ensure appropriate restrictions are placed over the interception platform to ensure integrity and confidentiality is maintained. The OIC of SOAU and/or ADO will ensure all documentation submitted by IAU for section 180 and TI warrants are secured in a manner as to restrict/prevent access by unauthorised staff. SOAU will make such records available for ombudsman inspection as required.
rti|tele-data-and-The-Special-Operations: SOAU may provide information on the different types of data that can be obtained through a data authorisation. Examples include: Basic subscriber – customer name, date of birth, billing address, date of connection/disconnection. Call records – calling party (A), called party (B), time, date, duration and type of call. Other call record types include: Cell ID location (identify base station details using a cell ID as the search criteria) Cell dump (identify all calls made through a cell tower. A quote must be obtained from Optus and Vodafone/TPG before an authorisation is made – (Quote not to be requested pursuant to s178). EBM/VLR/GPS (near real time location of mobile if switched on and roaming). Complex subscriber – All the information contained in a basic subscriber but the requesting officer must include details of the additional information being sought e.g. copy of contract.
rti|tele-data-and-State-Operations-Contr: The SOCC provides 24/7 support to frontline WA Police Force Operations and have the capability to facilitate the following telecommunications data functions: Prospective Data Applications (authorisations and provisioning). Location Based Services (authorisations and provisioning). IPND checks In accordance with the s5AB(1) delegation schedule, the SOCC Inspectors provide 24/7 access to Authorised Officers for frontline officers and case officers. Case officers may submit telecommunications data authorisation applications for consideration by an Authorised Officer via the SOCC any time a local Authorising Officer is unavailable. SOCC Detective Sergeants will assist case officers in completing applications or when urgent circumstances exist a verbal briefing may be facilitated in order to expedite the application process. In any instances where SOCC facilitate the provisioning of a telecommunications data request, all documentation required for compliance is required to be maintained and made available for inspection by the ombudsman when required. All telecommunications data authorisations processed and facilitated by SOCC must be performed in accordance with the specific guidelines as outlined in this document, especially in relation to: Authorising Officer delegation. Authorising Officer considerations. record keeping and reporting. Journalist information, and Ombudsman inspection. Although the SOCC may implement internal procedures and processes in relation to telecommunications data authorisations, all processes and procedures must be in accordance with the WA Police Telecommunications Data and Authorising Officers Standard Operating Procedures. Internal Affairs Unit (IAU) IAU perform a number of telecommunications data authorisations outside of the SOAU and SOCC related to internal investigations conducted on behalf of the WA Police Force. Specific positions held within the IAU are provided delegated authority pursuant to the s5AB(1) schedule and as such may authorise telecommunications data requests submitted pursuant to Sections 178, 178A, 179 & 180. of the Act. All telecommunications data authorisations processed and facilitated by IAU must be performed in accordance with the specific guidelines as outlined in this document, especially in relation to: Case officer obligations. Authorising Officer delegation. Authorising Officer considerations. Record keeping and reporting. Journalist information, and Ombudsman inspection. Although the IAU may implement internal procedures and processes in relation to telecommunications data authorisations in order to prevent and restrict access to information sought and obtained, all processes and procedures must be in accordance with the WA Police Telecommunications Data and Authorising Officers Standard Operating Procedures.
rti|tele-data-and-Data-obtained-outside-: Each area within the WA Police Force responsible for submitting telecommunications data requests, must ensure upon receipt of any telecommunications data from a service provider, appropriate vetting is conducted of the data received to confirm: Data/information received is within the parameters of the authorisation date/time. Any data/information received identified as being outside of the parameters of the authorisation must be immediately quarantined. The appropriate quarantine register is updated to reflect the details of the quarantined data and why it was quarantined. Re-submit request to carrier seeking data only within authorised parameters. Make available quarantined data and register for inspection by Ombudsman as required. SOAU staff will maintain the Quarantine Register of all data received which is outside of an authorisation. Should a case officer have used data provided which is identified as being outside of an authorisation, he or she must quarantine such data, contact SOAU and seek legal advice immediately.
rti|tele-data-and-Data-Vetting: Areas within WA Police responsible and capable of submitting and receiving telecommunications data under Sections 178, 178A, 179 & 180 of the Act, must incorporate and demonstrate a process for vetting received data to ensure information/data provided by the carrier is within the parameters of the authorisation prior to releasing it to the case officer. Data identified as outside of the authorisation shall be immediately quarantined and not provided to the case officer (refer Data obtained outside of an Authorisation).
rti|tele-data-and-Quarantine-Process: SOAU have access to the quarantine repositories located within IDM. Quarantined – Unused Telecommunications Data Once investigators have finished vetting the results of cell tower and payphone data dumps and Payphone CCR’s / Reverse CCR’s to limit the intrusion to privacy of uninvolved parties, they must notify the SOAU Intel and Data Team, as per the process hereunder. Quarantined – Unauthorised Telecommunications Data To be used by a SOAU vetting officer when data is returned outside of the scope of the original request. At any time, a staff member, case officer or other identifies or requires telecommunications data to be quarantined, the member will contact the SOAU Intel and Data Team and: Provide reference number (IDM allocated number). Advise data to be quarantined. Advise which folder the data is to be locked down into. Seek email confirmation from IMU once task completed. Email SOAU and advise data has been quarantined (for case officers). Should access be required to this data at a later date a request in writing must be submitted via SOAU for approval.
rti|tele-data-and-Revocation: An Authorising Officer or any Case Officer, must revoke a prospective authorisation as soon as he or she becomes aware the grounds for originally issuing the data authorisation have ceased to exist (section 180(7)). Upon a decision to revoke a prospective authorisation, the case officer must inform SOAU to facilitate the revocation, inclusive of a formal email. Once the investigator is satisfied the use of the Prospective Data is no longer required they must request the revocation of the authorisation: Send a request to revoke the authorisation to SOAU via the section email (Special Operations Application Unit mailbox: Mbx.SOAU@police.wa.gov.au). Warrant Administration staff will then disable the Operation/Target/Line on the JSI Interception System (WA Police Force Interception Platform). Warrant Administration staff log into the SOAU “Warrant Management System” and complete a 180 Prospective Revocation for the relevant Authorisation. Once completed this will generate a Section 180 Revocation document for signing by the Authorising Officer. Once signed, the revocation is communicated to the telecommunications carrier. Warrant Administration staff then notify the investigating officer that the authorisation has been revoked. Should SOAU receive a signed authority for Prospective Data that doesn’t meet the required legislative standard: Email the investigator “The submitted application requires further attention prior to provisioning with the carrier.” The email specifies that “should these issues not be rectified; the application will be subject to revocation pursuant to s180(7) of the Act.” If the matter is not resolved please complete Revocation Certificate pursuant to s180(7) of the TIA Act and have signed by Authorised Officer. Please advise applicant and file application with revocation certificate. (See compliance checklist.) SOAU Officer: _______________________ Date: __________________________ An authorised application may be subject to formal revocation for the one of the following reasons: Significant administrative error identified within the application. The reasons/grounds for the application have ceased to exists or changed to the extent the application is no longer required or requires a new submission. In each occasion where an authorisation is subject to formal revocation, a copy of the revocation certificate and documentation are to be forwarded to SOAU where the revocation and documents will be retained for inspection as required.
rti|tele-data-and-Use-and-Disclosure-of-: It is an offence to use or disclose any information which would reveal the existence of a telecommunications data authorisation (s180) or to use or disclose a document or information which has been disclosed to a person under a data authorisation. However, there are exceptions to these offences for enforcement of criminal law. In order to ensure that any use or disclosure of information is done for a permitted purpose, the Act requires the WA Police to keep records of use and disclosure of information in relation to telecommunications data authorisations and telecommunications data obtained under a s180 authorisation. The records in relation to the disclosure of telecommunications data authorisations or telecommunications data for the purpose of the enforcement of criminal law are kept by the case officer, using the WA Police Use and Communications Log (UCL) template. The information to be recorded in the template includes: The disclosure or use that took place. When the disclosure or use took place. The basis on which the disclosure or use falls within one of the exceptions. The Act enables the use or disclosure of information or documents if: the disclosure or use is for the purposes of the authorisation, revocation or notification concerned; or the disclosure or use is reasonably necessary for the enforcement of the criminal law. for the enforcement of a law imposing a pecuniary penalty; or for the protection of the public revenue. There are other use and communications responsibilities relating to authorisations obtained under s178, s178A or s179 for existing information or documents (historic information) within s181B and s182 of the Act, which must be recorded as per section 186A of the Act (Secondary Use and Communications).
rti|tele-data-and-Prospective-Data-PD-Ap: WA Police members and Authorised Officers are required to demonstrate consideration of certain and specific matters when submitting and authorising a Prospective Data Application pursuant to s180 of the Act. (see hereunder) Within the WA Police, SOAU and the SOCC are permitted and have the required access, training and systems to provision Prospective Data Applications. (SOCC access is via s287 for Persons at Risk) No other business areas are permitted to perform this function.
rti|tele-data-and-Case-Officer-2: In addition to the details of the service number, the case officer submitting a Prospective Data request must include the following information for consideration by the Authorising Officer: If the request relates to Journalist Information. Relevant offence under investigation (> 3 years imprisonment). Duration of request (< 45 days). Evidence of current use/possession of service by the suspect. IPND/Subscriber results of service number (address if different to suspect). Confirmation of understanding that the request must be revoked as soon as the reason for the request no-longer exists.
rti|tele-data-and-Authorising-Officer: The Authorising Officer upon reviewing the application submitted must take into consideration several factors and further, must demonstrate consideration of these factors in approving the application. The factors which require specific demonstration of consideration are: The Authorising Officer holds a position as per s5AB(1) delegation schedule. That the disclosure is reasonably necessary for the investigation. Privacy considerations have been satisfied, as per section 180F of the Act. Current use/possession of the device/number has been satisfied. If the application relates to Journalist Information, and Reason for approval/rejection of application. A prospective data application is only authorised once the Authorising Officer endorses the application with a signature (hard copy or electronic, not verbal) also recording the date and time of approval. No data may be obtained under the authorisation prior to the date and time recorded against the authorised officer’s signature. Data obtained prior to the date and time the authorisation was made (notified) is unauthorised and must be quarantined immediately and the relevant quarantine register updated. Should data be obtained prior to notification to the carrier, and be used by a WA Police Force member, it must be immediately quarantined and legal advice sought. A case officer should seek an Authorising Officer from within his/her district or division in the first instance however, in circumstances requiring immediate or urgent processing the SOCC provides 24/7 365 access to Authorising Officers to review and authorise an application.
rti|tele-data-and-Location-Based-Service: WA Police members and Authorised Officers are required to demonstrate consideration of certain and specific matters when submitting and authorising a Location Based Service Application pursuant to s180 of the Act (listed hereunder). Within the WA Police the Special Operations Application Unit and State Operations Control Centre are permitted and have the required access, training and systems to provision Location Based Service Applications. No other business areas are permitted to perform this function.
rti|tele-data-and-Case-Officer-3: In addition to the details of the service number and target details, the case officer submitting a Location Based Services request must include the following information for consideration by the Authorising Officer: If the request relates to Journalist Information. Relevant offence under investigation (> 3 years imprisonment). Evidence of current use/possession of service by the suspect, and Evidence of current possession/use of device/service. Confirmation and understanding that the request must be revoked as soon as the reason for the request is no longer valid. A location-based service application is only authorised once the Authorising Officer endorses the application with a signature (hard copy or electronic, not verbal) also recording the date and time of approval. No data may be obtained under the authorisation prior to the date and time recorded against the authorised officer’s signature. Data obtained prior to the date and time the authorisation was made is unauthorised and must be quarantined immediately and the relevant quarantine register updated. Should data obtained prior to authorisation have been used by a WA Police Force member it must be immediately quarantined and legal advice sought. A case officer should seek an Authorising Officer from within his/her district or division in the first instance, however, in circumstances requiring immediate or urgent processing the SOCC provides 24/7 365 access to Authorising Officers to review applications. Access to LBS data is subject to secondary use and communication restrictions, as per the Act.
rti|tele-data-and-Authorising-Officer-2: The Authorising Officer upon reviewing a location-based service application must take into consideration several factors and further, must demonstrate consideration of these factors in approving the application. The factors which require specific demonstration of consideration are: The Authorising Officer holds a position as per s5AB(1) delegation schedule. That the disclosure is reasonably necessary for the investigation. Privacy considerations have been satisfied, as per section 180F of the Act. If the application relates to Journalist Information. Current use/possession of the device/number has been satisfied, and Reason for approval/rejection of application. A location-based service application is only authorised once the Authorising Officer endorses the application with a signature (hard copy or electronic, not verbal) also recording the date and time of approval. No data may be obtained under the authorisation prior to the date and time recorded against the authorised officer’s signature. Data obtained prior to the date and time the authorisation was made is unauthorised and must be quarantined immediately and the relevant quarantine register updated. Should data obtained prior to authorisation have been used by a WA Police Force member it must be immediately quarantined and legal advice sought. SOCC authorised officers are provided with the ability (in urgent circumstances) to obtain a verbal briefing from a case officer. When considering a verbal briefing the Authorising Officer is required to make sufficient notes in order to demonstrate consideration and satisfaction of the required criteria prior to authorisation (the final authorisation must be in writing). The location-based services application form provides an area for an Authorising Officer to record notes given during a verbal briefing. The location-based services handbook provides direction and guidance in respect to location-based service applications and authorisation. No “ping” of a service number/device can occur prior to the Authorising Officer’s endorsement (including date and time, not verbal) of a location-based service application (pages 2 & 3). The investigating officer must inform SOAU by email of the required ping rate at the commencement of the Location-based Service and any subsequent changes to the ping rate. The Authorising Officer and case officer should record the considerations given to the setting and adjusting of the ping rate, which may be subject to variation throughout the operation. All documents and notes associated with a LBS application must be retained by the area provisioning the application (SOCC or SOAU) for ombudsman inspection.
rti|tele-data-and-Evidentiary-Certificat: An evidentiary certificate may be admitted in evidence as proof of its contents. Certain individuals who work for a carrier may issue an evidentiary certificate. A carrier’s evidentiary certificate may set out the facts concerning the acts or things done in giving effect to a data authorisation (s 185A(1)). If a case officer requires an evidentiary certificate, the case officer will submit a request via the IDM RFI request portal. An evidentiary certificate request should include: Carriage Service Provider. Date certificate required by. Original Law Enforcement Agency request reference. Original Carriage Service Provider reference. Original Request Type e.g CCR, subscriber check. Service identifier (number). An evidentiary certificate or court statement must not be submitted under a Chapter 4 Authority (178, 178A, 179 & 180). A case officer may seek advice from SOAU if assistance is required in obtaining and court statement of evidentiary certificate.
rti|tele-data-and-Manual-Data-Entry: The importance of entering correct information into WA Police systems and registers cannot be understated, errors and incorrect information result in inaccurate ministerial reporting on behalf of the WA Police. Regardless of the area within WA Police responsible for the provisioning and authorisation of telecommunications data requests, staff MUST make every effort to ensure: Information entered into all systems and registers is accurate and correctly identifies the relevant data authorisation. The relevant reference numbers and/or request type is entered correctly into all systems where required including SEDNode, OSTRAVA, RMS and IDM. The relevant reference numbers and/or request type is entered correctly into all WA Police registers including Quarantine and Revocation registers. Although a number of systems have been introduced to reduce instances of manual data entry errors, there is still a requirement at certain stages of telecommunications data authorisation and facilitation process which require manual information/data entry. Incorrect or inaccurate information entry will result in incorrect reporting and subsequently result in adverse findings from the oversight body (Commonwealth Ombudsman). When a critical error has been identified, it will be reported to the oversight body as soon as practicable for review during auditing (self-reporting). Where possible/applicable areas and staff should apply the appropriate measures to QA manual data entry to reduce/eliminate errors.
rti|tele-data-and-Reports-to-the-Ministe: The WA Police must report annually to the Minister on a number of matters associated with data authorisations (section 186). This report must be made as soon as practicable after 30 June each year, and within 3 months of 30 June at the latest. In particular, the WA Police must report on: The number of authorisations made; The offences in respect of which authorisations were made; The age of the data sought under an authorisation; The number of authorisations for subscriber information; The number of authorisations for traffic data; and The number of authorisations that were made under journalist information warrants. The Special Operations Application Unit will prepare these reports on behalf of the Commissioner of Police.
rti|tele-data-and-Record-keeping: The WA Police must keep the following records for a period of three years, or until the Ombudsman gives the Minister a report about the records, whichever is earlier (section 186A(3)): Data authorisations; Records which indicate whether authorisations were properly made, including considerations in relation to the privacy requirements set out in section 180F; Records showing that WA Police notified the relevant carrier of an authorisation Revocations; Records indicating whether revocations were properly made; Records showing that WA Police notified the relevant carrier of a revocation; Documents or materials indicating that any use or disclosure of data authorisation information or accessed data was lawful; Evidentiary certificates issued by WA Police authorised officers; and Reports given to the Minister under section 186.
rti|tele-data-and-Raw-Data-Dump-of-SEDNo: All areas of WA Police that access telecommunications data will retain sufficient primary records of each authorisation and notification to demonstrate compliance with s183 and s186A of the Act, including the requirements prescribed by the Determination. Primary records must be kept that demonstrate: The date and time an authorisation was notified; and The form and content of the authorisation that was given with the notification. A calendar invite is sent to each area’s responsible staff member to ensure this activity is undertaken monthly.
rti|tele-data-and-SEDNode-Access-Audit: Each area of WA Police accessing telecommunications data will each perform the following activity once per calendar month: Review and update staff within respective area with access to SEDNode and Telstra OSTRAVA/Rms: The nominated officer within each area to conduct a monthly audit and if staff have left the area advise Intelligence Systems Support SMAIL, to update the SEDNode users group, and advise Telstra via LELadmin@team.telstra.com A calendar invite is sent to each business area’s responsible staff member to ensure this activity is undertaken monthly.
rti|tele-data-and-Journalist-Information: If an Authorised Officer knows, or reasonably believes, that the information that will be disclosed by the authorisation may include information, of the data authorisation, would be: A person who is working in a professional capacity as a journalist, or an employer of such a person; and A purpose of making the authorisation would be to identify the journalist’s source. then the Authorised Officer must not issue a data authorisation unless a journalist information warrant is in force (section 180H).
rti|tele-data-and-Threshold-for-the-issu: Journalist information warrants are issued under section 180T of the TIA Act. An issuing authority may only issue a journalist information warrant if satisfied that the warrant is reasonably necessary for the enforcement of the criminal law, and the public interest in issuing the warrant outweighs the public interest in protecting the confidentiality of the identity of the relevant journalist source, having regard to: Privacy implications; The gravity of the matter; The extent to which the data would be likely to assist in the matter; Whether reasonable attempts have been made to obtain the information by other means; Any submissions made by a public interest advocate; and Any other matters that the issuing authority considers relevant. A warrant must be in place before an authorisation can be made if an authorised officer knows, or reasonably believes, that the subject of the data authorisation would be: A person who is working in a professional capacity as a journalist, or an employer of such a person; and The purpose of making the authorisation would be to identify the journalist’s source. Once a journalist information warrant is issued, an authorised officer may make a data authorisation under the authority of the warrant according to normal procedures, as set out above.
rti|tele-data-and-Notifying-the-Ombudsma: If a journalist information warrant is issued a copy of the warrant must be provided to the Commonwealth Ombudsman as soon as practicable (section 185D(5)(b)). If a data authorisation is made under the authority of a journalist information warrant, a copy of the authorisation must be provided to the Commonwealth Ombudsman as soon as practicable after the warrant has expired.
rti|tele-data-and-Entry-into-force-and-r: A journalist information warrant enters into force when it is issued (section 180V). It will remain in force for the period specified in the warrant, up to a maximum period of 90 days (section 180U). The WA Police Commissioner may revoke a journalist information warrant at any time by means of a signed revocation instrument (section 180W(1)(a)). The WA Police Commissioner must revoke a journalist information warrant if he or she is satisfied that the grounds on which the warrant was issued have ceased to exist (section 180W(1)(b)).
rti|tele-data-and-Commonwealth-Ombudsman: Under section 186B of the Act, the Commonwealth Ombudsman is entitled to inspect records which are required to be kept by WA Police under section 185 & 186 of the Act. Inspections by the Commonwealth Ombudsman The Commonwealth Ombudsman is required under Chapter 4A (sections 186B-186J) to inspect WA Police Force records to determine the extent of compliance with the data provisions of the TIA Act. The Ombudsman has extensive powers to enter premises and examine records and reports to the Minister about his or her inspections. Consequently, personnel from the Commonwealth Ombudsman office will attend WA Police Facilities periodically to inspect the records. The Ombudsman’s staff should have unrestricted access to WA Police Force records related to Telecommunications Information. WA Police Force staff must provide the Ombudsman’s inspectors with all necessary assistance to enable them to perform their duties. The Officer in Charge, SOAU will facilitate any visit by the Commonwealth Ombudsman for the purpose of record inspection, including providing access to Ombudsman inspection staff to WA Police ICT systems to enable the inspection to be conducted. Case officers who have requested access to data and authorised officers will make themselves available to inspectors at any time requested during an inspection. The Commonwealth Ombudsman will report to the Minister about the results of its inspections.
rti|tele-data-and-Compliance-Unit-Inspec: All WA Police business areas utilising telecommunications data and interception legislation may be subject to inspection by the Ethical Standards Division, Compliance Unit, to ensure ongoing compliance with legislative and policy requirements. Findings from the inspections will be reported to the business area’s Superintendent, Commander Standards and Legal Portfolio and the Commonwealth Ombudsman.
rti|tele-data-and-Authorisations-MUST-NO: An authorisation for sections 178, 178A, 179 and 180 of the Act must not be made under the following circumstances: An Authorising Officer is NOT satisfied that the request has met the requirements of sections 178, 178A, 179 or 180 of the Act. The request is for the CONTENT of a communication. This would require a warrant. The request is for the information of a journalist, journalist source or an employer of a journalist. This would require a warrant under section 180J. The request is for the purposes of a Coroner’s investigation. This requires a warrant from the Coroner’s Court under section 33(3) of the Coroners Act 1996. For the purposes of authorisations for Sections 178, 178A and 179 – if the request is for a FUTURE date (Prospective Data). This will need to be done through section 180. If the request is for telecommunications business records, not telecommunications products. This would require an order to produce. The request is for Telstra 000 recordings / audio. (Note: call register is acceptable). This must be under section 286 of the Telecommunications Act 1997. The request is for a Crime Stoppers call. This is protected under legislation and if in doubt liaison should be made with Crime Stoppers. The request is for a person /entity KNOWN to the authoriser (conflict of interest) This must be referred to either the Inspector or Superintendent for decision of signature as well as whether to refer to Internal Affairs if the request concerns a Police Officer or Staff member. The request is for an Evidentiary or Court Certificate. This does not require Chapter 4 Authorisation.

rti|tele-remo-syst-1-REMOTE-ACCESS-TO-TE: It is the intention of the Western Australia Police Force (WA Police Force) to allow authorised police officers and staff remote monitoring access to lawful telecommunications interceptions in accordance with legislative requirements. Remote access is defined as any access to any telecommunications interception platform from an area external to Special Operations Application Unit (SOAU).
rti|tele-remo-syst-STANDARD-OPERATING-PR: The purpose of these Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) is to communicate: Types of remote interception platforms; Procedures for obtaining remote access to Lawful Interception Information; Specific security requirements; Compliance; Security requirements and retention of records; Good Governance requirements for Detective Offices and business areas; and Summary.
rti|tele-remo-syst-1-1-TYPES-OF-REMOTE-A: JSI Telecom is the provider of the Telecommunication Interception (TI) platform to the WA Police Force. It provides separate applications for investigators and analysts to access lawfully intercepted TI information (LII) obtained under warrant (TI service warrants and named person warrants) and metadata (data) obtained under TI Authorisation (prospective data and location-based service).
rti|tele-remo-syst-4SIGHT-UCM-UCM: UCM is the primary interception platform for the WA Police Force and can be accessed by remote desktop connection via a computer that has been approved for access by SOAU. Access to UCM is limited by the number of licences available to the WA Police Force and in general each remote access facility will only have one or two UCM enabled computers. UCM is utilised by Officers to live monitor, live map, review intercepted content and metadata, update the workflow of a session or for any data entry that is required (such as document summaries, updating associate details in the Name Number Index as examples). UCM is also required for investigators to create evidence sets for use and disclosure purposes and for resetting JSI passwords for all applications. Application for UCM access is to be made via the local District Office and forwarded to SOAU for consideration and approval by Inspector, Crime Support and Services, State Crime. Approval will be subject to availability of UCM system licenses and a link speed test of the connection into the premises to ensure there is no degradation of other WA Police Force network services. UCM users can access Speech-To-Text transcription and multilingual translation of intercepted content.
rti|tele-remo-syst-4SIGHT-EXPLORER-4SE: 4SE is a desktop application that is available for download via the software centre. Access to the application is managed within UCM and requires users to have a current JSI account and to maintain currency of the Telecommunication Interception Compliance course located on the eForce learning platform. The WA Police Force implemented 4SE in 2020 to complement the existing UCM platform. With its user friendly and visually driven interface, 4SE promotes in-depth analysis from all intercepted sessions and data types. The filter panel and perspective views expand on the filtering options that can be generated in 4Sight UCM. 4SE users can access Speech-To-Text transcription and multilingual translation of intercepted content.
rti|tele-remo-syst-4SIGHT-LOCATOR-4SL: 4Sight Locator is a mobile application that allows real-time or historical viewing of target location information using an WA Police Force mobile device. When your device is registered and enabled on 4Sight UCM, 4Sight Locator uses an encrypted data connection between the mobile device and 4Sight UCM so that you can access your target data. You can display live or historic location information for one or multiple lines for different targets at the same time. The target’s location information is updated as new data is collected on the 4Sight UCM system. Users need to be mindful of the security of the device when accessing the 4SL platform away from the secure office environment. When using WA Police Force mobile devices all users need to be aware of and comply with the following: AD-71.00 Information Systems and Security Policy; AD-71.04 Remote Access to Police Information Systems Policy; AD-71.09 Acceptable Computer Use Policy; CO-01.24 Mobile Devices; and WA Police Force Code of Conduct and local business area SOPs.
rti|tele-remo-syst-1-2-PROCEDURES-FOR-AP: Remote access is defined as any access to telecommunications interception platform from an area external to SOAU. The detective business unit must establish a secure monitoring environment, manage identified risks and comply with the legislation governing intercepted communication. These services will only be provided to approved business units when the standards below have been met: The monitoring environment meets the standards set in this document [refer herein section titled Specific Security Requirements]. The approved members have completed the Telecommunication Interception Compliance course located on the eForce learning platform, have a current JSI account and have been given lawful access to operations containing TI warrants or authorisations.
rti|tele-remo-syst-1-3-SPECIFIC-SECURITY: The following specific security requirements will be assessed in any consideration of a facility for remote interception access. The computer must only be used in a secure office environment with only persons permitted to access the LII or data, present. The computer monitor must be fitted with headphones and must be used when monitoring audio. Persons not registered at SOAU for the Operation being intercepted or data authorisation may not monitor, or be present during access, unless it has been lawfully disseminated in accordance with the act. All information obtained, used and disseminated from the interception must be recorded on the Restricted Record Register.
rti|tele-remo-syst-1-4-COMPLIANCE: The Commander, State Crime or their delegate (Compliance Unit), is empowered by the Commissioner to ensure compliance to legislation and this policy. The purpose of the Ethical Standards Division, Compliance Unit, is to provide an independent auditing and assurance function to business units mandated to applying covert investigative methodologies located within the Crime Support and Services Division (CSS). The unit will ensure that State Crime Command are compliant in regards to the State and Commonwealth legislation compliance requirements. The Commander, State Crime, or their delegate is required to enter upon police premises operating remote monitoring facilities and: inspect the physical security of the listening room / office environment; inspect the storage of Records; inspect any other relevant records held; and ensure compliance with the legislation by the business unit. The inspections may be unannounced, and the Compliance Unit are to be afforded immediate and unhindered access to the telecommunications interception monitoring facility and to the security storage area or areas where restricted records are held. The Management Audit Unit will conduct critique inspections in accordance with Good Governance Guide requirements. The results of these audits will be provided to the Compliance Unit, for follow up and to the Risk Assurance Committee, as per the agencies audit policy.
rti|tele-remo-syst-Non-compliance-to-Leg: A breach of legislation or procedures may result in a criminal or disciplinary proceeding. Breaches may result in the withdrawal of access to the Telecommunications Interception Platform or the cessation of the interception warrant.
rti|tele-remo-syst-1-5-SECURITY-REQUIREM: [Section 8 (1) of the Telecommunications (Interception and Access) Western Australia Act 1996 (WA)] “Investigators are required to store their records in a secure place where it is not accessible to persons other than persons who are entitled to deal with it.” The case officer must retain the below records: Original written or electronic records of lawfully intercepted information; Each use made by the agency of lawfully intercepted information; Each disclosure of lawfully intercepted information by an officer of the agency; and Each occasion when lawfully intercepted information was produced in a judicial proceeding.
rti|tele-remo-syst-1-6-GOOD-GOVERNANCE-R: Applies to Detective Offices and business areas approved by SOAU. Required minimum tasks to be completed: (i) Ensure relevant staff have completed the annual Telecommunication Interception Compliance course located on the eForce learning platform. (ii) Ensure headphones or similar are used when listening to live lines or recorded information.
rti|tele-remo-syst-1-7-SUMMARY: SOAU have decentralised live telephone interception. This has given investigators timely access to interceptions, allowing them to coordinate dynamic operations in “real time”. The procedures have been designed to increase officer’s awareness to the interception legislation and procedural requirements. Adherence to these procedures will reduce the incidence of intercepted evidence being excluded from judicial proceedings and reduce non-compliance risks. Should you have any queries please contact the SOAU Manager on 08 9223 3511.
rti|tele-remo-syst-2-LEGISLATION-GUIDELI: The SOAU business unit previously held responsibility within this agency for the interception of live communications. Increasing demand for SOAU services has dictated a shift to remote access monitoring by approved registered officers within their own business units (JSI access granted). These guidelines are designed to detail the legislative and procedural obligations, which apply to members engaged in remote access monitoring and reviewing. Remote access monitoring is the process where SOAU provides the technical capability to monitor an intercepted communication and the case officer is responsible for monitoring, reviewing and managing the product. These procedures are intended to complement and reinforce the relevant responsibilities and record keeping functions carried out by the WA Police Force when executing warrants under the Telecommunications (Interception & Access) Act 1979 (Cth) (the Commonwealth Act) and complying with the Telecommunications (Interception and Access) Western Australia Act 1996 (WA) (the State Act).
rti|tele-remo-syst-The-Commonwealth-Act-: To protect the privacy of individuals using telecommunications in this country, by making it an offence to intercept communications passing over the telecommunications networks [section 7(1) of the Commonwealth Act]; and To allow the lawful interception of communications in certain circumstances by law enforcement and intelligence agencies.
rti|tele-remo-syst-Section-46-of-the-Com: Where an agency applies to an eligible Judge or nominated AAT Member for a warrant in respect of a telecommunications service and the Judge or nominated AAT member is satisfied … that information that would be likely to be obtained by intercepting under a warrant, communications made to or from the service would be likely to assist in connection with the investigation by the agency of a serious offence. Serious Offence in general terms is an offence that is punishable by imprisonment for life or for a minimum period of 7 years and meets a specific criteria as defined by the Act [a serious offence is explicitly defined in section 5D of the Commonwealth Act]. Lawfully Intercepted Information (LII) can only be used for a Permitted Purpose [the definition of a permitted purpose is contained within section 5 of the Commonwealth Act] and states that, in general terms, LII can be used for the purposes of an investigation by the agency or eligible authority of a Prescribed Offence. A Prescribed Offence in general terms is the investigation of an offence that is punishable by imprisonment for a minimum of 3 years.
rti|tele-remo-syst-USING-INTERCEPTION-IN: In the event that an investigator discovers another Prescribed Offence during the course of an interception it may be used in the subsequent investigation. It cannot be used for offences that do not meet the Prescribed Offence definition as detailed in the legislation. The investigator should use caution when using interception information for this purpose. Further disclosure can only be made for a Permitted Purpose. An officer investigating the original offence can use interception information to investigate a Prescribed Offence. An officer investigating the original offence can disclose interception information to another investigator not involved in the original investigation, to allow the investigation of the Prescribed Offence. An officer investigating the original offence who wishes to disclose to another agency, must do so by liaising with SOAU in compliance with the provisions of section 68 of the Commonwealth Act.
rti|tele-remo-syst-INVESTIGATOR-DISSEMIN: An investigator is empowered to communicate information in the following circumstances: Section 67(1) of the Commonwealth Act allows: (1) An officer or staff member of an agency may, for a permitted purpose, or permitted purposes, in relation to the agency, and for no other purpose, communicate to another person, make use of, or make a record of the following: (a) lawfully intercepted information other than foreign intelligence information; (b) interception warrant information. This communication is to assist the investigator to conduct the investigation and includes enlisting an interpreter, translator and other police officers and must be within the constraints of the legislation.
rti|tele-remo-syst-COMMUNICATING-RESTRIC: Section 68 of the Commonwealth Act, empowers the Commissioner or a person authorised by the Commissioner to communicate lawfully intercepted information to another interception agency in certain specific circumstances. No officer, unless subject to a section 68 authorisation from the Commissioner, may communicate information to an external agency. Contact the Officer in Charge of SOAU for any interagency communication.
rti|tele-remo-syst-Telecommunications-In: Section 63 of the Commonwealth Act, prevents the communication of intercepted product in contravention of Section 7. If you are investigating a secondary offence of Indecent Assault, with a penalty of 2 years imprisonment, this offence falls short of the threshold for prescribed offences which is 3 years imprisonment. The intercepted information cannot be used to progress an investigation into the secondary offence, no further communication is allowed to any other person. Lawful Interception information is not to be used for populating intelligence databases, not to be placed on Statement of material facts, Briefing notes or Incident reports. Not to be copied into WAPOL systems such as Silva, Teams, WebEOC, Outlook. Interception information may only be used for a permitted purpose - using interception information for intelligence purposes is a breach of the Commonwealth Act. Intercepted information can only be accessed by the investigation team (including supervisors of the original investigation) and then only disclosed further for a permitted purpose.
rti|tele-remo-syst-Section-105-of-the-Co: (1) A person who contravenes subsection 7(1) or section 63 is guilty of an offence against that subsection or section. (2) An offence against subsection 7(1) or section 63 is an indictable offence and, subject to this section, is punishable on conviction by imprisonment for a period not exceeding 2 years.
rti|tele-remo-syst-USING-INTERCEPTION-IN: In the event that an investigator discovers another prescribed offence during the course of an interception, it may be used in the subsequent investigation. It cannot be used for offences that do not meet the prescribed offences definition, pursuant to Section 5 of the Commonwealth Act. The investigator should use caution in using interception information for this purpose. Further disclosure can only be made for a permitted purpose. In summary: An officer investigating the original offence can use interception information to investigate a prescribed offence. An officer investigating the original offence can disclose interception information to another investigator not involved in the original investigation, to allow the investigation of the prescribed offence. An officer investigating the original offence who wishes to disclose to another agency, must do so by liaising with SOAU OIC or Manager in line with the provisions of section 68 of the Commonwealth Act [refer herein, section titled, Communicating restricted information to another interception agency].
rti|tele-remo-syst-3-INVESTIGATOR-RESPON: The investigating officer needs to ensure the following: At the commencement of an operation the investigator is responsible for completing the Investigator Notification Sheet for SOAU monitoring staff which includes: Officer contact details / on call officers, etc. Objectives of the operation / profile of the target, POI’s. Operational phrases / key words / associates / meetings of interest, etc. Explanation of what SOAU can do for investigator. The IO needs to be in regular contact with SOAU to supply operational updates [if unable to attend in person an email to Station Mail will suffice] Arrange regular review of screened call sessions, supply names of officers responsible for reviewing the calls so they can be added to the operation. Prompt interpretation of foreign language calls if applicable See Speech-To-Text and Translation in Section 4. As a security measure, if contacted by a staff member of SOAU to relay information during the operation: SOAU Member says: “Message from the lobby”; and Investigator replies with their: “Name, rank & regimental number” If they don’t get that response, the SOAU staff member will hang up immediately. Storage of all TI product / associated paperwork, etc. is to be in a safe/lockable cabinet. Investigator is to immediately disclose to SOAU any issues of corruption or misconduct by notifying the Interception Supervisors on 9223 3550. Prompt notification to SOAU via e-mail must be done should a warrant no longer be required so that it can be revoked. Completion of an effectiveness report for each warrant must be done no later than seven days after the warrant’s termination/revocation.
rti|tele-remo-syst-4-TELECOMMUNICATION-I: Currently SOAU is maintaining 4 models of interception:
rti|tele-remo-syst-SOAU-MONITORED-DIRECT: In this model SOAU maintains responsibility for managing the intercepted product and will compile a brief summary of each call intercepted. Investigators will have access to all intercepted product and it is the responsibility of the investigator to review each session and select the appropriate classification and review status [refer section titled Review Status and Classifications hereunder]. The investigator can also access the SOAU Monitored model, but must advise the supervisor on duty at SOAU of their intention. The SOAU monitors will not review or complete summaries of the intercepted product relevant to the specified operation whilst the investigator is accessing the product, as it will disrupt the continuity of the intercepted sessions. It is the investigators responsibility to act as a monitor, reviewing the product, compiling a summary and selecting the appropriate classification and review status [refer section titled Review Status and Classifications hereunder]. On completion the investigator must advise the SOAU supervisor that they have ceased monitoring to enable the SOAU monitors to resume interception. SOAU will notify the investigator by phone of any information of note or specifically requested by the investigator. If the information intercepted is deemed to be of a critical nature by SOAU the investigator will receive a phone call and email advising them of the information intercepted. If the investigator uses discretion to mitigate an offence, it is their responsibility to submit a discretionary report.
rti|tele-remo-syst-SOAU-MONITORED-FILTER: In this model SOAU maintains responsibility for managing the intercepted product and will compile a brief summary of each call intercepted, however SOAU will withhold from the investigator intercepted product that they are precluded from by a condition of the warrant or by the request of the investigator. An example of this would be where a condition has been placed on the warrant by a Judge precluding the investigator from having access to certain product such as legal privilege calls. Therefore, in this case all calls deemed by SOAU to be legal privilege would be withheld from the investigator. It remains the responsibility of the investigator to review all other sessions and select the appropriate classification and review status [refer section titled Review Status and Classifications hereunder]. SOAU will notify the investigator by phone of any information of note or specifically requested by the investigator. If the information intercepted is deemed to be of a critical nature by SOAU the investigator will receive a phone call and email advising them of the information intercepted. If the investigator uses discretion to mitigate an offence, it is their responsibility to submit a discretionary report.
rti|tele-remo-syst-DIRECT-ACCESS-INVESTI: In this model SOAU facilitates the technical capability to intercept telecommunications and it is the responsibility of the investigator to monitor and manage the intercepted product. It is also a requirement that the investigator compiles a brief summary on JSI of each call intercepted and selects the appropriate classification and review status [refer herein section titled Review Status and Classifications].
rti|tele-remo-syst-SPEECH-TO-TEXT-AND-TR: SOAU have implemented Speech-To-Text transcription and translation technology through JSI. This transcription is available to view in both UCM and Explorer programmes on 4sight. The Transcription and Translation documents, can be located on the ‘documents’ tab of the session within the session details. Language will automatically be set to English, unless otherwise detected through the JSI translation programme, the languages detected will be populated onto the result. The results also show a percentage as to the confidence on the transcriptions accuracy. SOAU staff have the capability to re-run the session in another language and should be contacted if this is required. The investigating officer is to assess the product produced and determine if it requires professional translation. PLEASE NOTE: Any AI-generated translation or transcription is considered an intelligence product only. It must not be used as evidence, disclosed or copied outside the JSI system, or acted upon operationally until the content has been verified by directly examining the original source material (e.g., audio or text from the intercepted session).
rti|tele-remo-syst-Corruption-Misconduct: If an investigator uncovers any session of “Corruption/Misconduct” nature including allegations of the investigators attached to the relevant case. The investigator must immediately advise SOAU Interception Supervisor by telephone and as directed, e-mail the details of the Operation Name, Warrant Number, Session Number, and a brief synopsis of the allegation/s contained within the session directly to that Interception Supervisor. The SOAU Interception Supervisor will review and advise Internal Affairs if necessary.
rti|tele-remo-syst-Legal-Privilege: The JSI status of the session must be designated “Legal Privilege”. Intercepted calls between the person of interest and their legal representative for the purpose of communicating with their client or gain instructions to act for that client for legal matters, is deemed to be legal professional privilege. A legal representative includes a solicitor, barrister, a member of their staff or an agent acting on their behalf. This information must not be disseminated or acted upon, it is a common law immunity to preserve the confidentiality of legal communications. Legal professional privilege cannot be attached to communications for the purpose of facilitating a crime or there is a higher public interest. It is recommended that direction be sought from WA Police Force, Legal Services before acting upon any communication that has the potential to be defined as legal professional privilege.
rti|tele-remo-syst-Risks: If the intercepted communication identifies a risk of injury to persons, damage to property or the commission of an offence. The investigator is to immediately notify their supervisor to decide what action is to be taken. If the case officer uses discretion to mitigate an offence, it is their responsibility to submit a discretionary report.
rti|tele-remo-syst-Interpretation-Foreig: When a foreign language call is intercepted, the following steps must be followed to ensure appropriate review and operational use: Review the AI Translation Investigators should first review the AI-generated translation available in the JSI system. This translation is considered an intelligence product only and must not be used as evidence or acted upon operationally without verification. Determine Need for Professional Interpretation If the content of the call is required for evidentiary purposes or operational action, a professional interpreter must be engaged through the agency’s approved translation service process. Engage Translation Services Submit a request for interpretation via the existing agency process. If assistance is required, contact SOAU staff for support in initiating or managing this process. Upload Summary to JSI Interpretation Panel Once the professional interpretation is complete, a summary of the call should be placed in the JSI system’s interpretation panel. Mark as ‘Interpretation Complete’ The interpreted call must be classified as ‘Interpretation Complete’ in the system. This ensures SOAU staff are notified and can proceed with reviewing the interpreted content. Interpreters are subject to confidentiality agreements to access LII, so please liaise with SOAU if this is required. WARNING – The accuracy of the JSI translation cannot be verified without a professional translation service.
rti|tele-remo-syst-CLASSIFICATIONS: Not Classified – system default for new calls; SOAU monitors to review. Investigator Review – for investigator to review. Foreign – for investigator to arrange interpretation. Review - Relevant – session believed to be relevant to operation. Review - Not Relevant – session not believed to be relevant to operation.
rti|tele-remo-syst-REVIEW-STATUS: The Review Status should update automatically as the session Classification is changed. Designators used are: Not Viewed – system default for new calls; SOAU monitors to review. Investigator Review Required – for investigator to review. Completed – call has been reviewed by an investigator. Interpretation Required – used to identify sessions requiring interpretation, once interpretation completed investigator must select appropriate review status – arranging an interpretation is the responsibility of the investigator.

rti|virg-airl-Overview: LAW ENFORCEMENT INFORMATION REQUEST Virgin Australia Airlines Pty Ltd (Virgin Australia) is willing to assist agencies performing law enforcement functions and the regulatory objectives of the government by providing passenger details and other information in accordance with the Privacy Act 1988 (Cth).
