ryj|aip-inst-guid-GENERAL-INSTRUCTIONS: 1. Access the Automated Interview Plan (AIP) via the WA Police Intranet home page via Forms, then Fill in a Form. 2. The Automated Interview Plan appears in the list of forms accessed from the homepage. 3. The other access pathway is via the Investigative Standards intranet site, via the WA Police Intranet site > The Job > Investigative Standards > Investigative Interviewing. The link shown on this page will direct the user straight to the AIP. 4. Enter information via the first screen: a. Incident Report Number (ddmmyy hhmm nnnnn). b. Interviewee’s Name and date of birth (dd/mm/yyyy format). c. Interviewer’s Name. d. Corroborating Officer’s Name (if not yet known, duplicate the Interviewer’s details). The interviewee’s date of birth will prefill the ‘Interviewee Information’ for Adult or Child. e. Make selections applicable to the circumstances of your interview. The below example illustrates the selection of Adult with the Interviewee Status of Arrested Suspect. The information detailed in the grey boxes detail the selections made in this example.
ryj|aip-inst-guid-INTERVIEW-DETAILS: Incident Number 190721 1045 11559 Interviewee’s Name Joe BLOGGS Interviewee’s Date of Birth 01/01/1970 Interviewer’s Name SCHULBERGS, Marika [PD11006] Corroborating Officer’s Name SHELTON Joanne [PD11717]
ryj|aip-inst-guid-INTERVIEW-CONSIDERATIO: Yes selections to the following: - Is there an interpreter This selection will activate another selection area of ‘Language nominated’ and in some instances another selection field of ‘Was Pre- recorded Caution used’. All other considerations are indicated to No. Pre-recorded Caution Planning initiative for another project, awaiting implementation.
ryj|aip-inst-guid-INTERVIEWEE-INFORMATIO: ‘Yes’ selections to the following: Aboriginal or Torres Strait Islander Person. All other considerations are indicated to No. 5. The next screen is the ‘Interview Plan’ (only applicable for ‘Interview Status’ of ‘Arrested Suspect’ or ‘Accompanying Person’). The user has a choice to enter the planning component of the ‘Interview Plan’ electronically, or opt to manually complete this after the AIP has generated. Here you can complete the planning component of your suspect/accompanying person interview, including Police Agenda Steps, Evidence and Challenges. 6. The next screen will display a summary of selections made. For example, if your interviewee is an ‘Aboriginal or Torres Strait Islander Person’, and you did not select ‘Interview Friend’ as a consideration, this will appear in red text as a reminder to address the requirement. It must be emphasised there are considerations that must adhere to legislative or case law requirements, such as an interview of a juvenile. In other instances, you can continue without changing the consideration selections, but you must document your rationale on your running sheet, so the decision can be explained at a later date. In this example, it may be that the consideration has been addressed by the interviewer, but is not required in this instance (e.g. Arrested Suspect did not wish for an Interview Friend to be present). a) For corrections to any of your previous selections, click on the button marked ‘Previous’ and make the relevant choices, dependant on the circumstances of the interviewee. Or b) If all displayed selections are correct – Preview the information. 7. At this stage you can ‘Preview’ the information and forms generated into the document, which is based on the selections made. This is the last opportunity to make changes to the information selected or to amend incorrect text entries. Use the ‘Exit’ button to move back through the screens to make the required amendments. Note: the information will display with no formatting to check the information selections. This is the last opportunity to make any amendments. 8. Select ‘Print’ and the document will generate as a PDF. The interview plan will appear as a PDF document which you should ‘Save As’ to your office ‘P’ drive (or agency endorsed equivalent) under the appropriate folder for your investigation. a. A message box will display at the bottom of the screen requesting whether you wish to ‘Open, Save or Cancel’. b. Choose the ‘Save’ option. i. Select the down arrow to the right of the word ‘Save’ ii. Select ‘Save as’ to your office ‘P’ drive/equivalent under the appropriate folder for your investigation iii. Name the document c. If you choose the ‘Save’ option, the PDF will automatically save to your ‘Downloads’ folder; or d. Choose the ‘Open’ option i. The document will automatically name ‘AIP-[Interviewee Name]-[Date generated]’ and will be stored to the download folder on your computer, e.g. ‘AIP-Joe+Bloggs-19072021.pdf’. If you have any questions or recommendations for this application please contact Investigative Standards Unit.
ryj|aip-inst-guid-EXPLANATION-OF-SCREENS: Arrested Suspect or Accompanying Person Screen 1- Front Cover Enter relevant information via the first screen 1. Interview Details a. IR Number ddmmyy hhmm nnnnn b. Interviewee’s Name Name of the interviewee c. Date of birth dd/mm/yyyy format (Determines interviewee as Adult or Child) d. Interviewer’s Name Populates to the log-in details of the user d. Corroborating Officer’s Name Search using surname (pre-emptive text field), or if corroborator is unknown, duplicate interviewer’s details. 2. Interview Status (only one choice is permitted) a. Arrested Suspect; b. Accompanying Person; or c. Witness (not applicable for this interview status). 3. Interviewee Information (this is determined from the details entered for date of birth) a. Adult; or b. Child. Plus a ‘Y/N’ response to any combination of the following: c. Aboriginal or Torres Strait Island Person. d. Culturally or Linguistically Diverse. e. Suspected to have Foetal Alcohol Spectrum Disorder (FASD). f. Suspected mental impairment. g. Physical impairment which may impact on communication. h. Suspected involvement in recent emotional/traumatic incident. i. Suspected recent drug/alcohol use. 4. Interview Considerations (only the relevant fields applicable to the Interviewee Information are available) a. Is there a responsible adult. b. Is there an independent person. c. Is there an interview friend. d. Is there an interpreter (this selection will activate another selection area of ‘Language nominated’ and in some instances an additional selection field of ‘Was Pre-recorded Caution used’. i. Language nominated (applicable to selection of ‘Interpreter’). ii. Was Pre-recorded Caution used (applicable to selection of Aboriginal or Torres Strait Islander Person, and this field is required for future enhancements). All the above listed fields require completion or the user will not be able to progress past Screen 1. Screen 2 – Suspect Interview (This screen only appears when Arrested Suspect/ Accompanying Person selected) The user has the option of completing the ‘Planning’ requirements within the AIP: a. Electronically; or b. Manually. Screen 3 - Summary This screen will provide a summary of the selections made by the user. Where there is a requirement to consider an option from Interview Considerations and this selection is not made, there will be information indicated in red text to warn the user that the associated relevant option has not been selected. An example of this a. Where ‘Culturally or Linguistically Diverse’ is selected on the initial screen; and b. ‘Is there an interpreter’ has not been selected on the initial screen. This may have been an oversight with the initial selections, and the user has the option to go to the ‘Previous’ screen to amend the selections. OR The user may have determined that an interpreter is not required, and can progress to the next stage of the application. In this instance it is recommended the rationale and decision be recorded to the associated running sheet. Screen 4 – Preview of AIP prior to generating The AIP is viewable in a ‘Preview’ format. a. The user has the capability to read or scan through the content of the entire document. b. If the user notes changes to be made, there is a capability via the ‘Exit’ button to go to previous pages within the application to amend selections. c. If the user determines the AIP is correct to proceed, progress to the final screen via the ‘Print’ button. Important to note - Once the AIP is sent to print (generated PDF) the user will not be able to add or amend any information. Screen 5 – Generated AIP document A PDF document will be generated. This document requires a ‘Save As’ to name and save to the designated electronic document repository (business unit drive). The generated AIP will: a. Produce a cover sheet listing: i. IR Number ii. Interviewee’s Name. iii. Interviewer’s Name. iv. Corroborating Officer’s Name. v. Date of interview. vi. Name of Person compiling. vii. Date (indicates when the form was generated). b. Produce and include information relevant to the selected ‘Interviewee Information’ (dependent on choices made) in the listed order: i. Aboriginal or Torres Strait Island Person. ii. Culturally or Linguistically Diverse. iii. Suspected to have Foetal Alcohol Spectrum Disorder (FASD). iv. Suspected mental impairment. v. Physical impairment which may impact on communication. vi. Suspected involvement in recent emotional/traumatic incident. vii. Suspected recent drug/alcohol use. c. Provide forms relevant to the ‘Interview Considerations’ and the sequence of interview. Information entered on the ‘Front Cover’ screen will populate into the relevant areas in the forms: i. IR Number. ii. Interviewee’s Name. iii. Interviewer’s Name. iv. Corroborating Officer’s Name.
